_comment: Core 10e attack-sequence damage allocation. Attacks are resolved/allocated one at a time. A model that has already lost wounds (or had an attack allocated this phase) must keep receiving further attacks until it is destroyed before allocation moves to a new model. When a model is destroyed, the killing attack's excess damage is LOST and has no effect - it does NOT carry over to another model. Therefore the number of models a unit can destroy is bounded by the number of unsaved wounds (allocations), never by the damage total: three unsaved wounds of Damage 6 destroy at most three one-wound models. SwegHammer models one Unit per model, so the target's same-squad_id siblings are the rest of the codex unit; the allocation pointer in Unit.attack advances to the next surviving sibling only after the current model dies. Devastating Wounds in current 10e is a save-bypassing NORMAL hit and is governed by this same allocation rule (excess still lost, no cross-model carry) - it is NOT a mortal wound. True mortal wounds DO carry over to another model and are a separate mechanic, not routed through this pointer.

simulator.damage_allocation_spillover.quoted_text: If the target unit contains a model that has already lost any wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase, the controlling player must allocate further attacks to that model until either it is destroyed, or all the attacks have been saved or resolved. ... If a model loses several wounds from an attack and is destroyed, any excess damage inflicted by that attack is lost and has no effect.
simulator.damage_allocation_spillover.trigger: an unsaved wound (or a save-bypassing Devastating Wound) is allocated to a model in a multi-model target unit
simulator.damage_allocation_spillover.effect: the allocated model loses wounds equal to the Damage characteristic; if it is destroyed the excess damage is lost, and the next unsaved wound is allocated to the next surviving model of the same unit, so total models destroyed is bounded by the number of unsaved wounds, not the damage total
